# Extreme Continuation Expansion

The Awtsmoos renews each pixel from nothing, every instant bright;
Awtsmoos.com must reveal each vessel clean, on desktop and mobile light.
Not novelty for novelty, not redesign for show;
Only where the interface obstructs the user shall refinement grow.

## Expanded mission

The previous pass proved that shallow geometry can lie when styles are still loading. This continuation therefore becomes more exacting: every apparent defect must be supported by source evidence plus readiness-aware runtime evidence, or by a source contradiction so direct that runtime behavior cannot reasonably rescue it.

## New audit dimensions

- Route readiness: `document.readyState`, stylesheet rule availability, script/resource settlement, and stable geometry snapshots.
- Responsive geometry: 320, 375, 390, 430, 768, 1024, 1440 widths where representative.
- Vertical constraints: 568, 667, 844, and desktop heights for short-screen clipping.
- Interaction state: closed/open menus, drawers, dialogs, dropdowns, command palettes, game HUD overlays, settings panes.
- Layer model: fixed/sticky elements, transforms, filters, opacity, isolation, contain, backdrop-filter, and portal placement.
- Focus model: visible focus, keyboard reachability, hidden focusable elements, off-canvas focus traps.
- Touch model: critical controls below roughly 40px, hover-only actions, dense clusters, edge controls under mobile safe areas.
- Scroll model: body/document overflow, nested scroll ownership, locked scroll, clipped scrollbars, canvas capture.
- Typography model: overflow from long labels, unbreakable URLs, monospace panes, dynamic localization-like strings.
- Game model: canvas scaling, HUD overlap, touch controls, orientation assumptions, fixed score/status panels.
- Editor model: toolbars, resizers, split panes, sidebars, tab strips, terminal panes, command surfaces.
- Shared-shell model: global nav/header/footer, authentication banners, notifications, toasts, overlays.

## False-positive defenses

1. Wait for app styles to be parsed before measuring.
2. Reject offscreen elements that are deliberately closed or hidden.
3. Reject honeypots and accessibility skip links unless focus behavior is broken.
4. Reject decorative world backgrounds larger than viewport unless they create document scroll or cover controls.
5. Reject horizontally scrollable editor toolbars when the scroll mechanism is discoverable and controls remain reachable.
6. Reject external redirects as layout defects.
7. Do not call a fixed element clipped when its owning state is intentionally off-canvas.
8. Do not infer touch failure from size alone; verify importance and density.
9. Do not infer z-index failure from magnitude alone; verify overlap order.
10. Do not change global CSS for an isolated issue.

## Aggressive evidence targets

The strongest candidates are surfaces that combine at least two of:

- source-wide structural risk;
- runtime overflow after style settlement;
- inaccessible primary controls;
- actual overlap of visible interactive rectangles;
- short-height clipping;
- open overlay escaping viewport;
- focusable elements trapped under or behind overlays;
- fixed/sticky collisions;
- mobile controls obscuring game/editor content;
- shared component defect affecting multiple consumers.

## Completion standard

No cosmetic victory counts. The pass closes only after: all structural scan categories are harvested; highest-risk candidates are source-traced; representative apps/games/pages are measured after readiness; each proven issue is fixed by complete-file rewrites; changed files are reread; tests/build/syntax run; before/after runtime checks pass; and the final remaining-work ledger contains no safe evidence-backed UI/UX repair in scope.
